title: Prefix hit projection notebook and staged safe-apply for KV caching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a lightweight, reproducible notebook and safe staged-apply procedure that: (1) models per-prefix hit elasticity against TTL changes and cache key normalization, (2) produces recommended TTL knobs and canonicalization rules for high-value prefixes, and (3) defines a traffic-gated canary + rollback plan with clear metric guards for production apply.
background: We frequently under-tune TTLs for low-latency prefixes and over-cache noisy keys (user IDs, timestamps) which creates wasted memory and increased write amplification. Existing guidance is scattered across playbooks; this ticket centralizes a quantitative workflow: sample traces, build a hit-elasticity model, synthesize TTL deltas, and apply changes via a staged rollout with automated safety gates.
proposed_changes:
1) Notebook that consumes request traces and outputs per-prefix hit curves and marginal benefit (tokens saved / extra memory cost) for TTL deltas.
2) A small set of canonicalization rules (normalize query params, strip volatile session fragments, group by logical bucket).
3) Staged apply orchestration: shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metric gates at each stage.
4) Alerting templates and a dashboard to monitor regressions during rollout.
hit_model_summary: We will estimate hit-rate as a function h(T) where T is TTL using stratified bootstrap over a 14-day window. The model computes: baseline hit, projected delta for TTL+/-k, and confidence intervals. We will calculate marginal cost-savings per TTL-second by combining token counts, per-token cost, and additional memory footprint. For sparse prefixes, use Bayesian smoothing to avoid overreacting to noise.
ttl_tuning_heuristics:
- Target hits-per-kb uplift > 0.2 before increasing memory budget.
- For high-frequency prefixes (>10k q/day), allow larger TTL increases but enforce p50 p99 latency gates.
- Limit TTL change per rollout step: max 2x TTL or +3600s, whichever is smaller.
- For unknown prefixes, prefer low-risk TTL increases (e.g., +30s) and collect 3 days of metrics before enlarging further.
cache_key_guidelines:
- Canonicalize by removing ephemeral query params (utm_*, session_token).
- Normalize timestamps to coarse buckets (minute/hour) only when semantics allow.
- Hash long request bodies using stable hashing to avoid key explosion.
- Add 'canonical_version' suffix to keys for quick rollback and auditability.
- Avoid customer PII in keys; use deterministic pseudonymous IDs if required.
rollout_plan:
1) Dry-run shadow for 24h comparing cache hits and downstream load.
2) Canary 1% traffic for 1 hour; check gates.
3) Expand to 5% for 3 hours; check gates.
4) Expand to 25% for 24h; run full regression evals.
5) Full 100% apply.
Each stage is automatic: a failing gate halts expansion and triggers an automated rollback to previous config.
rollback_triggers:
- Sustained increase in p99 latency > 10% for 10 minutes.
- Error rate increase (5xx) > 0.5% absolute.
- Cost per request increases > 5% sustained across 30m window.
- Hit-rate drops for targeted prefixes by > 8% absolute and not explained by traffic shifts.
- Functional correctness regression detected by prompt-set evaluation (any decline beyond noise band).
observability_and_gates: Metrics to monitor: per-prefix hit rate, cache eviction rate, cache size by prefix, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, tokens per op, downstream DB RPS. Dashboards: TTL-change diff view, canary comparison charts, and a realtime alert for gate violations. Gating rules are expressed as threshold checks with 3-minute rolling windows for latency and 30-minute windows for economic signals.
experiment_and_eval_plan:
1) Generate cohorted request samples (hot, warm, cold) from the 14-day trace.
2) Run synthetic replay to compute counterfactual cache behavior for +/- TTL adjustments.
3) Validate model predictions on a separate holdout day and compute prediction error.
4) Run small production shadow and compare predicted vs observed hit deltas.
5) If errors > 15% for hot prefixes, tune smoothing priors and rerun.
notes_and_open_questions:
- Need to decide default smoothing prior for low-frequency prefixes.
- Confirm how canonical_version will be surfaced in console rollout UI.
- Determine retention window for per-prefix counters used by models (7d vs 14d).
- Engineering cost estimate for adding per-prefix memory breakdown to /metrics endpoint.
